_meta.goal: cap and recover the remaining cost leaks: idle polling between dispatches, a hung agent burning the full timeout, phantom/lost receipts in the cost ledger, a spend ceiling, and the spec drift round 7 introduced

tasks.title: Wake the dispatcher the moment an attempt finishes instead of sleeping through the poll interval (a_finished_task_wakes_the_dispatcher_immediately)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn a_finished_task_wakes_the_dispatcher_immediately' tests/wakeup.rs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL (cost/makespan): make the dispatcher wake the instant an attempt finishes instead of sleeping through its poll interval. Right now a finished task's worker slot sits IDLE until the poll timer expires.

BUG (measured on the current binary): `run::run_loop` ends each iteration with `std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(poll.max(1)))`, and `reap()` only drains the completion channel with `rx.try_recv()`. So a completion is noticed up to `poll_secs` late. Probe: 2 tasks chained A -> B, `max_parallel=1`, `TF_POLL=30`, and an agent stub that takes ~0s. Expected if work were the only cost: ~1s. MEASURED: 60.4s elapsed, exit 0 - i.e. two full 30s sleeps (one per dispatch) wasted on zero work. At the default `poll_secs = 15` that is ~15s of dead time per dispatch, and it compounds on every serialized chain.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR:
1. The wait for a completion must be interruptible. Introduce a blocking receive with a timeout on the existing completion channel (`mpsc::Receiver<(String, String, Outcome)>`): `rx.recv_timeout(d)` wakes immediately when a task finishes, and still returns after `d` so nothing else changes.
2. Preserve `poll_secs`'s remaining meaning: it stays the UPPER BOUND on how long the loop may idle before re-evaluating (so deadlock detection, self-heal and any edge case still get re-checked on schedule). Do not remove the timeout re-evaluation entirely - just stop sleeping when there IS news.
3. Recommended shape (keep it small and readable): give `reap` an extra parameter, e.g. `wait: Option<Duration>`, that FIRST does `rx.recv_timeout(wait)` and handles the received message, then drains the rest with the existing `try_recv()` loop. The loop then calls `reap(.., Some(Duration::from_secs(poll.max(1))))` and the trailing `sleep` is DELETED. The `--once` path keeps polling with its short 200ms sleep - pass `None` there so it keeps its current semantics.
4. No behaviour change beyond the wake-up: exit codes stay exactly what they are today (0 all-done, 2 deadlock/config error, non-zero on failure), the dispatch order/`max_parallel`/`--task`/`--worker`/`--once` semantics are unchanged, and the deadlock path must still fire when nothing is running and nothing is ready. A task that is still running must still be waited for; never busy-spin (the timeout bound is what prevents that).
5. Watch the borrow/ownership details: `reap` takes `&mut router` and `&mut status`, and the channel receiver is shared with the spawned attempt threads via `tx`. Do not clone the `Receiver` (it is not `Clone`) and do not wrap it in a mutex - the loop is the single consumer.

TEST - new file tests/wakeup.rs, `#[test] fn a_finished_task_wakes_the_dispatcher_immediately()`. Model the harness on `tests/e2e.rs`'s `fixture()` helper (copy the pattern rather than importing it: a scratch git repo under a uniquely-named temp dir with `git init -b main` and repo-local `user.name`/`user.email`, a tasks.json + workers.json written to temp files, `agentflow::config::load(...)`, and a `Settings` built by hand pointing `cli` at `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_example_agent")`). Then:
   - set `poll_secs = 30` and `max_parallel = 1` on the Settings you build, with TWO tasks where B depends on A (a serialized chain, so there are two dispatches and two waits);
   - set `agent_timeout_s` low (e.g. 60) and `accept_timeout_s` low (e.g. 10), and use a trivial gate (the stub writes DONE.txt by default, so `test -f DONE.txt` passes for A; give B a gate that cannot fail, e.g. `true`, since its branch may carry no new commit);
   - time `agentflow::run::run_loop(&cfg, &st, &RunOptions::default())` with `std::time::Instant`, assert it returns 0 and that BOTH tasks are `Done`;
   - assert the elapsed time is BELOW a threshold that is IMPOSSIBLE to reach while sleeping through a poll interval - `poll_secs` is 30 and there are two waits, so assert `elapsed < Duration::from_secs(20)`. Add a comment stating the measured numbers: 60.4s before the fix, ~1-2s after.
   Make it hermetic: unique temp dir per test, cleaned up at the end, `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` set for the fixture repo. No new dependencies.
DO NOT BREAK: tests/e2e.rs (`self_heals_stale_running_state`, `restart_after_partial_run_skips_done_and_continues_remaining`, `retry_after_gate_failure_runs_fresh_attempts_until_it_passes`), the `src/run.rs` unit tests, and the `--once` path.

tasks.title: Kill an agent that stops producing output instead of burning the whole agent_timeout_s (a_stalled_agent_is_killed_before_the_total_timeout, a_stall_window_does_not_disturb_a_healthy_agent)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn a_stalled_agent_is_killed_before_the_total_timeout' tests/watchdog.rs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL (cost): stop a HUNG agent from burning the entire `agent_timeout_s`. Today the only bound is the total timeout, which defaults to 3600 (an hour of paid tokens) - and agentflow has no way to notice that the agent has stopped producing output, because it never looks at the output until the child exits.

BUG (code-confirmed in src/subprocess.rs): `run()` spawns reader threads that call `so.read_to_string(&mut s)` / `se.read_to_string(&mut s)` - a single blocking read that only returns at EOF - and the polling loop only compares `start.elapsed() > timeout`. There is no activity signal, so a stalled agent is indistinguishable from a working one until the full timeout expires.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR:
1. Add an OPTIONAL stall watchdog. Keep the existing `pub fn run(...)` signature and behaviour EXACTLY as-is: add a sibling `pub fn run_with_stall(cmd: &str, args: &[String], cwd: Option<&Path>, env: &[(String, String)], env_mode: EnvMode, timeout: Duration, stall: Option<Duration>) -> CmdOut`, make `run(...)` delegate to it with `stall: None`, and add `CmdKind::Stalled`. (Do not change the existing signature - it has callers in gate.rs, worktree.rs, run.rs and tests.)
2. Activity tracking: replace each reader's single `read_to_string` with an incremental chunked loop (`std::io::Read::read` into a fixed buffer, appending to the local String, breaking on `Ok(0)` or `Err`) and publish a "last output" timestamp after every non-empty chunk. Share it as an `Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>` holding millis elapsed since an `Instant` anchor created BEFORE the readers are spawned. The main loop computes `idle = anchor.elapsed() - max(last_stdout, last_stderr)` and, when `stall` is `Some(d)` and `idle >= d`, kills the child, waits, classifies the result as `CmdKind::Stalled`, and breaks. The final stdout/stderr must still be the full captured output.
3. Preserve the no-deadlock property: the incremental read must keep draining the pipe (that is what prevents a child that writes more than a pipe buffer from blocking). `tests/contract_gate.rs` has a 256 KiB no-deadlock test - it MUST keep passing. Do not assemble output by reading only once.
4. Post-kill handling: a killed child's orphaned grandchildren can hold the pipe write ends, so joining the readers can block. The existing timeout path already handles this by taking a 200ms grace and SNAPSHOTTING the buffers instead of joining. The stall path must do the same - do not join after a stall kill.
5. Configuration: add `pub agent_stall_s: u64` to `Settings`, sourced from `TF_AGENT_STALL_S` with default 0. **0 means DISABLED (legacy behaviour, exactly today's)**, so every existing caller/test is unaffected unless it opts in. `execute.rs` must call `run_with_stall(.., if ctx.st.agent_stall_s == 0 { None } else { Some(Duration::from_secs(ctx.st.agent_stall_s)) })` for the AGENT CLI ONLY - leave the git and acceptance-gate calls on plain `run(...)` (a silent gate is not necessarily a stalled one, and changing gate behaviour would break the timeout contract tests).
6. The failure must be DIAGNOSABLE and distinct from a total timeout: when the agent is stalled, the attempt's outcome/receipt error must say the agent produced no output for N seconds (name the configured stall window). Extend the existing agent-failure classification in execute.rs rather than adding a second failure path; keep the existing "agent exited {kind} (code {code})" text for non-stalled failures, because `tests/e2e.rs::failed_receipt_carries_the_failure_reason` asserts it contains "agent exited" and the exit code.
7. Add a knob to the stub agent `src/bin/example_agent.rs`: `FAKE_AGENT_HANG_MS` - sleep that long BEFORE writing any output, so a test can produce a genuine stall. Cap it the way `FAKE_AGENT_SLEEP_MS` is already capped (do not allow an unbounded sleep). Put it next to the existing sleep knob.

TESTS - new file tests/watchdog.rs (build the harness the same way tests/e2e.rs::fixture does; you may set process env vars for the stub - the agent child only receives keys listed in `TF_AGENT_ENV_PASSTHROUGH`, so set that list to include the FAKE_AGENT_* knobs you use):
1. `#[test] fn a_stalled_agent_is_killed_before_the_total_timeout()`. Build Settings with `agent_timeout_s = 60` and `agent_stall_s = 1`; set `FAKE_AGENT_HANG_MS` so the stub produces NO output for much longer than 1s (e.g. 30000). Time `run_loop`. Assert: it returns non-zero (the attempt fails - expect 2), the task is NOT `Done`, the recorded failure names the stall (assert on the receipt `error` via `Store::load_receipts()`, or on the task's `last_error`), AND the elapsed time is far below the 60s total timeout (`elapsed < Duration::from_secs(20)`) - that gap is the whole point: the stall window caught it, not the total timeout. Comment the measured contrast.
2. `#[test] fn a_stall_window_does_not_disturb_a_healthy_agent()`: with `agent_stall_s = 1` and the stub producing output immediately and exiting, the run still succeeds (exit 0, task `Done`) - prove the watchdog does not kill working agents, and that the default `agent_stall_s = 0` is genuinely disabled.
Keep the tests hermetic (unique temp dirs, cleanup, git identity env) and std-only - no new dependencies.

SCOPE-REVIEW NOTE (added mid-campaign; this task previously FAILED a scope check for exactly this reason). Adding a field to `Settings` is a CROSS-CUTTING change: `Settings` is built with struct literals in several files, and every one of them stops compiling the moment a field is added. You are authorised to edit ALL of them; do not try to avoid the Settings field to stay inside a narrow scope, and do not leave any literal stale. The struct-literal constructors are: `src/config.rs` (`from_env`), `src/execute.rs` (in-module test, around line 701), `src/run.rs` (in-module test, around line 1202), `tests/cli.rs` (~line 71), `tests/e2e.rs` (~line 71), `tests/journal.rs` (~line 85), `tests/scope_enforcement.rs` (~line 73), `tests/state_strict.rs` (~line 52), and `tests/wakeup.rs` (~line 101). Set the new field to its DOCUMENTED DEFAULT at every existing site, so no existing test changes meaning. Keep the change mechanical at those sites.

tasks.title: Write receipts atomically and stop the loader counting half-written temp files or silently dropping torn ones (receipt_writes_are_atomic_and_temp_files_are_never_counted, a_torn_receipt_is_reported_not_silently_dropped)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn receipt_writes_are_atomic_and_temp_files_are_never_counted' tests/receipt_atomic.rs && grep -q 'fn a_torn_receipt_is_reported_not_silently_dropped' tests/receipt_atomic.rs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL (data integrity): make receipt writes atomic so a crash can never leave a truncated receipt, and make the loader impossible to fool with a half-written file. Receipts are cost history: silently losing one undercounts what a campaign cost, and silently counting a phantom one inflates both spend and worker trust.

BUGS (both reproduced against the current binary). The receipts live in `<state_dir>/receipts/`, one JSON file per attempt.
1. `Store::append_receipt` (src/state.rs) does a plain `std::fs::write(path, data)` straight to the final path - no temp file, no rename, no fsync. A crash, SIGKILL, OOM or power loss mid-write leaves a TRUNCATED receipt on disk.
2. `Store::load_receipts` tries to parse EVERY file in that directory (`std::fs::read_dir` then `serde_json::from_str`) and `if let Ok(..)` SILENTLY SKIPS anything that does not parse. So (a) the truncated receipt above is silently dropped from the cost report and from the router's trust history, and (b) a leftover temp file that happens to contain valid JSON is COUNTED AS A REAL RECEIPT.
PROBE (3 files: 1 valid 100.0s receipt, 1 leftover temp file holding a valid receipt with attempt 2, 1 truncated receipt): `af cost` printed `TOTAL: 200.0s across 2 receipt(s)` with worker trust `w 2/2 1.00`. It double-counted the temp file as a second attempt (100.0s of phantom spend, phantom trust) and silently lost the torn receipt. This gets WORSE the moment you fix bug 1 naively, because an interrupted atomic write leaves exactly that kind of temp file behind - fix both together.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR:
1. Atomic append: write to a temp path in the SAME directory, fsync it, then `rename` it onto the final path (rename within one directory is atomic). Use the same discipline round 7 established for `run-state.json`: a UNIQUE temp name per write (a process-global atomic counter - never share one temp path between threads) and remove the temp file if any step fails. Reuse/read that code for the house pattern rather than inventing a second one.
2. The temp name MUST NOT end in `.json` (so it can never be mistaken for a receipt). Use e.g. `<final-name>.tmp-<pid>-<counter>`. Document the convention in a comment.
3. `Store::load_receipts` must only consider files whose name ends in `.json`. An interrupted write must therefore be structurally incapable of being counted.
4. Make the loss VISIBLE instead of silent. Add `pub fn load_receipts_checked(&self) -> (Vec<Receipt>, Vec<String>)` returning the valid receipts and one human-readable message per unreadable `.json` file that names the file (and the parse problem). Keep `pub fn load_receipts(&self) -> Vec<Receipt>` with its EXACT current signature, delegating and ignoring the second element, so no other file has to change. Do NOT make an unreadable receipt fatal - receipts are history; a corrupt one must not block a campaign.
5. Keep receipts sorted by `ts` as today, and keep the existing filename shape `<task>-<attempt>-<ts>-<nanos>x.json`.

TESTS - new file tests/receipt_atomic.rs (hermetic: a unique temp dir per test under its own per-test subdir, cleaned up at the end; use `Store::new(...)` directly, no git needed):
1. `#[test] fn receipt_writes_are_atomic_and_temp_files_are_never_counted()`:
   - many threads (>= 4) each append >= 50 receipts whose ATTEMPT NUMBERS ARE DISTINCT per thread (so final filenames cannot collide - do not rely on timestamp nanos for uniqueness); assert every append returns Ok, the directory then contains exactly that many `.json` receipts, every one of them parses, and `load_receipts().len()` equals the number appended;
   - assert NO temp files are left behind after the appends;
   - create a file matching the temp-name convention (`<something>.tmp-999`) containing VALID receipt JSON and assert `load_receipts()` does NOT count it (today it does - this is the double-count bug) while still counting the genuine receipts.
2. `#[test] fn a_torn_receipt_is_reported_not_silently_dropped()`:
   - put a truncated JSON file (e.g. `{"task":"A","attempt":3,"worker") in the receipts dir alongside valid receipts;
   - assert `load_receipts()` returns the valid ones and does not panic (history stays readable);
   - assert `load_receipts_checked()` reports the torn file BY NAME (the message must contain the file's name).
DO NOT BREAK: `tests/conformance.rs` (the generic `StateStore` suite calls `append_receipt`/`load_receipts`), the `src/state.rs` unit tests (`receipts_append_and_aggregate`, `legacy_receipt_without_outcome_is_merged`, and the phase tests), round 7's `tests/state_race.rs` and `tests/state_strict.rs`, and `run::cost`'s existing output shape (do not change `load_receipts`'s signature or sort order).

tasks.title: Reconcile the spec library with round 7's retry change: replace the now-false 'Retry with fresh branch' requirement with 'Scenario: gate failure retries only the gate' and document the af cost waste report
tasks.accept: grep -q 'Scenario: gate failure retries only the gate' openspec/specs/scheduling/spec.md && ! grep -q 'SHALL use a newly created branch' openspec/specs/scheduling/spec.md && grep -qi 'waste' openspec/specs/cli/spec.md && openspec validate --specs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL (spec/code agreement): reconcile the spec library with behaviour that round 7 changed. The implementation and its spec now CONTRADICT each other, and the traceability checker cannot catch it because it only verifies that a `// spec:` marker exists - not that the referenced test agrees with the scenario's prose. Fix the prose.

THE DRIFT:
- `openspec/specs/scheduling/spec.md` requirement **"Retry with fresh branch"** still reads: "A task SHALL allow up to `max_attempts` attempts (default from worker defaults). Each attempt SHALL use a newly created branch and worktree; a failed attempt SHALL NOT be retried on dirty state." with `#### Scenario: retry after gate failure` -> "WHEN a task's gate fails on attempt 1 and `max_attempts = 3` THEN the task is re-queued for a fresh attempt and runs at most 3 times total."
- The IMPLEMENTATION (round 7) deliberately changed this for the GATE case: a gate failure no longer deletes the attempt branch, and a retry whose branch already carries commits beyond the base branch attaches to that branch and re-runs ONLY the gate - it does NOT run the agent again. The bounded fallback: if the gate fails again on that reuse path the branch IS dropped, so the following attempt is a genuine fresh agent run. Scope violations, agent failures and merge failures still discard the branch as before.
- The tests that encode the new behaviour already exist and are green: `tests/e2e.rs::gate_flake_retry_does_not_rerun_the_agent` (asserts the agent runs exactly once - its own doc comment even says "Under the old always-fresh behavior the count was 2"), `tests/e2e.rs::gate_failure_keeps_the_agents_committed_branch` (asserts the branch survives a gate failure), and the pre-existing `tests/e2e.rs::retry_after_gate_failure_runs_fresh_attempts_until_it_passes` (the bounded-fallback path: gate fails twice, `attempts == 3`, receipts `failed/failed/merged`).

REQUIRED WORK:
1. Create the change with the native CLI: `openspec new change r8-spec-reconcile`. Author `proposal.md`, `tasks.md`, and the delta specs under `specs/<spec-id>/spec.md`. Then `openspec validate`, then archive it: `openspec archive r8-spec-reconcile --yes`.
2. CRITICAL, this has bitten us before: a `## MODIFIED Requirements` block is a FULL REPLACEMENT, not a patch. The replacement MUST reproduce every surviving scenario VERBATIM and then add/change the ones you mean to - anything you omit is SILENTLY DELETED. Read the whole current requirement (and count its scenarios) before writing the replacement, then verify afterwards that only the intended scenarios changed.
3. Rewrite the scheduling requirement so it matches reality. Rename it (the old name is now false) to something like `### Requirement: Retry reuses verified agent work`, and state the actual rule: up to `max_attempts` attempts; a GATE failure keeps the attempt branch and the retry re-runs only the gate (the agent is not re-invoked); a scope violation, agent failure or merge failure still discards the branch and re-runs the agent; if the gate fails again on the reuse path the branch is dropped so the next attempt is a fresh agent run. Include at minimum these scenarios, using these EXACT scenario titles so the traceability markers can reference them:
   - `#### Scenario: gate failure retries only the gate` (the agent SHALL NOT be re-invoked while the verified work survives)
   - `#### Scenario: gate failure keeps the verified branch`
   - `#### Scenario: a second gate failure falls back to a fresh attempt`
   - `#### Scenario: attempts are bounded by max_attempts`
   Write them in the GIVEN/WHEN/THEN style the rest of the library uses, and make each one's meaning match the test that backs it.
4. Traceability MUST stay green - `every_scenario_has_a_referencing_test` fails if a scenario has no marker, and a marker pointing at a slug that no longer exists is a dangling reference. The old slug `scheduling/retry-with-fresh-branch` (and the scenario slug `retry-after-gate-failure`) is referenced in `tests/e2e.rs` at lines ~279, ~1017, ~1018 and ~1075. Update EVERY one of those markers to the new requirement/scenario slugs, and add markers for the new scenarios onto the tests that actually prove them (`gate_flake_retry_does_not_rerun_the_agent`, `gate_failure_keeps_the_agents_committed_branch`, `retry_after_gate_failure_runs_fresh_attempts_until_it_passes`). Check `tests/spec_traceability.rs`'s allowlist (it is currently EMPTY - keep it that way if you can) and `docs/spec-traceability.md` for anything naming the old slugs, and run `cargo test --test spec_traceability` until it is green.
5. Also document the round-7 `af cost` waste output, which is user-visible but absent from the library: extend the `Cost report` requirement in `openspec/specs/cli/spec.md` so it states that `af cost` also reports WASTED spend - the seconds and attempt count of attempts whose outcome was not `merged`, the wasted percentage, and a breakdown grouped by failure reason - computed over the SAME receipt selection as the rest of the report (so `--last` / `--since` / `--task` narrow it too). Add a scenario for it and make sure it is backed by at least one existing test (`tests/cli.rs::cost_report_surfaces_wasted_spend` from round 7 is the natural one - add its marker).
6. Verify at the end: `openspec validate --specs` passes, `openspec list --specs` still shows the seven specs, and the requirement/scenario counts did not shrink unexpectedly. Report the before/after counts in your work.

The campaign's acceptance gate asserts that the ARCHIVED MAIN SPEC contains `Scenario: gate failure retries only the gate`, no longer contains the sentence `SHALL use a newly created branch`, and that `openspec/specs/cli/spec.md` mentions waste - so the archive must actually sync the changes into `openspec/specs/`.

tasks.title: Give a campaign a wall-clock spend ceiling that stops new dispatches and exits 3 (a_campaign_budget_stops_new_dispatches)
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn a_campaign_budget_stops_new_dispatches' tests/budget.rs && ./scripts/coverage-gate.sh && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
GOAL (cost control): give a campaign an actual SPEND CEILING. `agentflow` today has no budget of any kind - the only bounds are `agent_timeout_s` (3600) x `max_attempts` (3) x N tasks, so a runaway campaign can spend unboundedly with nobody able to say "stop after X". `af cost` already reports the campaign's consumed agent seconds as a TOTAL, so use that same number as the meter.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR:
1. Add `pub max_wall_clock_s: u64` to `Settings`, sourced from `TF_MAX_WALL_CLOCK_S`, default **0 = unlimited**. 0 MUST preserve today's behaviour byte-for-byte, so every existing campaign and test is unaffected unless it opts in.
2. Meter: the campaign's consumed budget is the SUM of `wall_clock_s` over the receipts in the state dir for the IN-SCOPE tasks - the same figure `af cost` reports as TOTAL. Reuse the existing receipt loading (`Store::load_receipts`) and the existing selection logic if it fits; do not invent a second meter and do not add a new persisted counter (the receipts already are the ledger, and they survive restarts, which is what makes the cap work across runs).
3. Enforcement in `run::run_loop`: before dispatching, if the measured spend is already at or above `max_wall_clock_s`, do NOT start any new attempt. Attempts already in flight must be allowed to finish (never kill a running attempt). Print a clear, single-line diagnostic naming the spend, the cap, and how many in-scope tasks were not started.
4. Termination: the budget stop must TERMINATE, not spin. Note the loop's existing structure: when nothing is running it checks whether any in-scope task is ready, and only reports a deadlock when none is. A budget-blocked ready task would keep that check happy forever, so handle the budget case explicitly - when the budget is what is preventing dispatch and nothing is running, return the budget exit code rather than looping.
5. Exit code **3** for "stopped early: wall-clock budget exhausted", documented in the README next to the existing exit codes, and distinct from 0 (done) and 2 (config error / deadlock). Do not reuse 2 - `tests/cli.rs` and `tests/e2e.rs` pin 2 for config errors and deadlocks.
6. Ordering/priority: a campaign whose in-scope tasks are ALL already `Done` must still exit 0 even when the measured spend exceeds the cap - completion wins over the budget. Only a run that actually has work left to start can report the budget stop.
7. `run::dry_run` should also surface the budget: when the measured spend already exceeds the cap, the plan must say so (a clear line; dry-run still creates nothing and still exits 0 - `cli/run-commands#dry-run` pins exit 0).

TESTS - new file tests/budget.rs, `#[test] fn a_campaign_budget_stops_new_dispatches()` plus focused companions. Build the harness the way `tests/e2e.rs::fixture` does (scratch git repo in a uniquely-named temp dir with repo-local git identity, tasks.json/workers.json in temp files, `agentflow::config::load`, a hand-built `Settings` whose `cli` is `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_example_agent")`, `agent_timeout_s` low, `accept_timeout_s` low, a trivial gate). Use the receipts directory as the meter: pre-seed it with hand-written `Receipt` JSON via `Store::append_receipt` (set `outcome` to `merged` and pick exact `wall_clock_s` values) so the spend is deterministic. Assert at least:
   - spend (e.g. 600.0s) >= cap (e.g. 500) with a ready task: `run_loop` returns **3**, the task is left `Ready` (not `Failed`, not `Done`), the base repo is untouched, and the agent was NEVER invoked - prove that last part by asserting the task's log file contains no `-- agent --` line (that marker is appended immediately before each agent spawn) or that the log does not exist;
   - spend BELOW the cap: the task is dispatched and completes (exit 0, `Done`);
   - `max_wall_clock_s = 0`: identical to today - the task runs and completes (the legacy guarantee);
   - all in-scope tasks already `Done` while spend exceeds the cap: exit 0, and nothing is re-dispatched (no new receipts) - completion wins over the budget;
   - the budget stop does not spin: the run with the exhausted budget returns promptly (assert the elapsed time is small, e.g. under 20s, with `poll_secs` set low like 1).
Keep the tests hermetic (unique temp dirs, cleanup) and std-only, no new dependencies.
DO NOT BREAK: the existing exit-code contracts (0/2), `tests/cli.rs`'s `run` tests, the deadlock path, `--once`, `--task`/`--worker` filters, and `src/run.rs`'s existing unit tests (including the round-7 `interrupted_attempt_consumes_the_retry_budget`).

SCOPE-REVIEW NOTE (added mid-campaign; this task previously FAILED a scope check for exactly this reason).
